subject: Phased GPU delivery & milestone billing — Icepeak Dedicated Ramp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhang <claire.z@icepeak.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Phased GPU delivery & milestone billing — Icepeak Dedicated Ramp

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Per our discussion, I'm putting a strawman here for a phased Dedicated capacity ramp for Icepeak so your procurement and finance teams can see the flow and the potential term discounts. Key goals we heard: predictable unit economics for Q1/Q2, minimize upfront cash exposure, and a path to a lower blended unit price if you escalate committed capacity later in year two.

Proposed ramp (example):
- Phase 1 (Q1): 30% of committed GPU capacity + baseline TPM allocation for inference peak windows
- Phase 2 (Q2): 60% cumulative capacity (add additional GPUs, increase token-throughput quota)
- Phase 3 (Q4): 100% capacity on agreed SKU mix (NVIDIA A100 / H100 options)

Billing options we can support today:
A) Annual prepay (renewing yearly): invoice up front for year, 10% term discount on list; staged delivery with monthly acceptance milestones and credits if delivered later than scheduled.
B) Multi-year prepays (36-month upfront): deeper discount (we can propose 16–20% depending on exact commit), with amortized credits tied to missed SLA or delivery shortfalls.
C) Hybrid: 50% year-1 prepay + 50% annual renewals thereafter; discount blended at ~12%.

A few asks from our side to make milestones practical:
- Define a clear acceptance test per phase (throughput/latency targets, KV cache behavior on your key workloads).
- Agree invoicing milestones (we usually invoice per phase delivery + final acceptance).
- Confirm target GPU SKU mix (we'll map to pricing tiers).

I've attached a term sheet and a sample invoice schedule that maps to the phases (Icepeak_Dedicated_Ramp_Termsheet_v3.pdf, Icepeak_Ramp_Invoice_Schedule.xlsx).

If the hybrid approach is preferable, we can tee up exact numbers and a credit waterfall that protects both sides. Happy to jump on 30 minutes tomorrow to run through numbers live.

Thanks,
Marissa
VP, Strategic Sales — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: Icepeak_Dedicated_Ramp_Termsheet_v3.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: Icepeak_Ramp_Invoice_Schedule.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Claire Zhang <claire.z@icepeak.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Phased GPU delivery & milestone billing — Icepeak Dedicated Ramp

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear outline. Procurement and finance here like seeing a phased delivery model, but cashflow is our primary constraint for the next two quarters. A few clarifying points / asks from my side:

1) Discounts: our CFO is pushing for a stronger incentive on multi-year prepay — is 16–20% the absolute range or is there room above 20% if we lock a specific GPU mix and a minimum annual spend floor?

2) Invoice timing: we cannot pay the full annual prepay in Q1. Can you support milestone invoicing where we pay 25% at Phase 1 acceptance, 35% at Phase 2, and 40% at full ramp? We'd prefer this with an annual renewal model (not an all-upfront 36mo prepay), but are open to a deeper discount if you require longer-term financing.

3) TPU/TPM mapping: our SRE asked what you mean by TPM in the strawman. For clarity, we'd prefer a tokens-per-minute (TPM) carriage rate tied to observed 99th percentile request rate — can we get an explicit table mapping TPM bands to additional GPU slices in the final commercial?

4) Legal & SOC2: we'll need SOC2 evidence and a short data residency note for EU traffic — can you provide SOC2 redacted and a short note on routing controls?

I'll loop in procurement and Ashwin (ops) on any follow-ups. Let's book time Friday to go over the numbers.

Best,
Claire Zhang
Head of Platform — Icepeak AI
claire.z@icepeak.ai

Claire —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. Quick answers and a counterproposal inline: 

1) Discount upside: If Icepeak commits to a 36-month prepay AND commits a minimum annual spend floor of $2.4M (aggregate across the three years), we can move to a 22% term discount on list pricing. That requires an all-upfront payment or an escrowed prepayment schedule; otherwise the discount steps down.

2) Invoice timing: We can absolutely support milestone invoicing inside an annual contract. For the hybrid/annual model you propose (25/35/40) we will accept the staged invoices but will attach a small financing premium (1.5% of the unpaid balance) to cover ramp provisioning risk if the full-year isn't prepaid. If you take the multi-year upfront, the financing premium is waived.

3) TPM mapping: we'll produce a 3-band mapping (Low/Med/High TPM) to GPUs and reserved KV cache. Karthik will include a recommended mapping once he validates your latency curves. We'll include that as an appendix to the term sheet.

4) SOC2 & routing: attaching SOC2 redacted; Redwood Private can pin EU traffic to a region and we can sign a routing addendum for any EU customer data flows. Neha will coordinate the SOC2 evidence and routing blurb.

Next steps:
- I'll update the term sheet with the 22% all-upfront number and a blended 10% annual-prepay number (with the financing premium callout).
- Karthik: could you add a short technical appendix with the TPM->GPU mapping and expected latency targets for Phase 1?
- Claire / Ashwin: if Q4 is a hard deadline for full capacity, tell us now so we can size delivery windows.

Can we lock a 30-minute slot Friday 10–10:30am PT to run through the numbers?

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachment: SOC2_cert_redacted.pdf (pdf)

Quick technical appendix to support the commercial mapping. High-level notes (for the term sheet appendix):

- TPM definition: tokens-per-minute measured at the 99th percentile of your production traffic sample. We'll baseline using a 72-hour window from a sample workload you provide.

- SKU mapping (example):
  * Low TPM band (<= 50k TPM): 1 x A100 equivalent per 250 rps baseline + 64GB KV cache slice
  * Mid TPM band (50k–200k TPM): additional A100/H100 fractional slices; recommend reserved burst pool for 2x traffic spikes
  * High TPM band (>200k TPM): H100 recommended with persistent KV cache + autoscale policy (burst into shared pool)

- Phase commitments: we recommend mapping Phase 1 to Low band capacity (30% of final GPUs) with a throughput acceptance test: 95% of requests < 120ms P50 and P99 < 450ms on your worst-case prompt set. Acceptance test harness details in the attached spreadsheet.

- Capacity smoothing: to reduce your committed GPU count we can apply quantization/compilation profiles suggested by Redwood Optimize; this typically reduces required GPU slices by ~15% for text-only workloads. Consider a proof-of-concept in Phase 1 for savings.

I'll attach a one-page mapping table to the term sheet. Happy to walk Icepeak's ops through the test harness during the Friday call.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Inference Engineering — Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Attachment: Ramp_Acceptance_Harness.xlsx (xlsx)

- Please provide a final invoice schedule matching the 25/35/40 hybrid flow (we'll need exact line items for PO).

- Please include a limited termination-for-convenience credit schedule (pro-rated refunds for a 180-day notice window) — our legal team requires this for procurement sign-off.

We can confirm a call Friday to finalize if Redwood provides an updated XLS with the invoice line items and a short legal summary of termination/credit mechanics. Also, please include the SOC2 redacted and routing blurb (we received the PDF but need an explicit one-paragraph routing addendum for EU traffic).
